text:
ella: Heads-up — PR #782 changes the example for GET /v1/models/{id}/metadata. It switches the example 'size' field from a number to a string. Need docs coordination before this lands. cc @sam @lee

sam: Which PR? link?

ella: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/782 — backend seems to accept both, but the example was edited to show "size": "1024" instead of 1024. Our OpenAPI schema still declares integer.

lee: Hmm. That will trigger our example/schema validation. We should not ship an example that contradicts the schema. Is the runtime actually returning strings for any models in prod?

ella: Looks like older checkpoints (pre-quantize conversion) return strings in metadata for size. Newer families return numbers. Runtime currently coerces, but consumers can be surprised.

nate: Product flagged this as nonbreaking, but QA saw a handful of customers parsing JSON strictly. We should document the variance and prefer the schema type in examples.

docs-bot: openapi-lint: example/type-mismatch: /components/examples/ModelMetadata.size expected integer but found string (example '1024').

sam: Proposed plan: revert the PR change so example shows an integer (1024). Add a small callout in the endpoint notes: "size may be returned as a string by some legacy models; runtime will coerce to integer where applicable." Add a short migration snippet for JS/Go.

lee: SGTM. For SDK snippets, include a tiny parse example: `const size = Number(metadata.size); // handles '1024' or 1024` and Go `sizeInt, _ := strconv.Atoi(metadata.Size)` as footnotes. Keep examples concise.

ella: I'll update the PR: revert example edit, add endpoint note, and attach snippets. Also will add a test file under /tests/examples/metadata-size-handling.md that demonstrates parsing both formats.

nate: Can you add a line in the release notes draft? "Docs: clarify model metadata 'size' example and add migration snippet for legacy string values."

sam: Small ask — add a one-line unit test to the examples CI so openapi-lint checks both example variants? Or at least ensure the canonical example matches schema.

ella: Will do. Pushing a commit in a few. Ping me for review @lee and @sam. :thumbsup:

lee: Thanks — I'll review quickly once updated.

sam: Marking this as docs-only, low risk. Merge after fixes and green CI. :eyes:
